page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-8 is a memory-configured virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 8 vCPUs mapped across 4 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 64.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-core allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. The machine includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and includes zero bundled public IPv4 addresses or GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate solid baseline compute and memory capabilities across varied operations. Stress-ng single-core execution delivers a score of 2,681.48, placing in the top quartile of tested instances, while multi-core processing reaches 10,764.32. PassMark testing yields an overall CPU score of 10,536.65 and an encryption metric of 8,375.72, supported by hardware AES and SHA extensions, though extended instruction benchmarks score in the lower quartile at 5,143.27 due to the absence of AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Memory bandwidth achieves 507.84 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read operations, 69.61 GB/sec on large 256 MB reads, and 46.34 GB/sec on large 256 MB writes. Real-world application throughput shows 7.66 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.24 GB/sec in static web serving.

The e2-highmem-8 profile offers favorable cost efficiency for workloads prioritizing memory footprint over raw multi-threaded throughput. With 64 GB of memory matched to 8 vCPUs, it caters to in-memory databases, Redis caches, mid-tier relational database management systems, and memory-intensive ETL tasks. Potential tradeoffs include reliance on external persistent disks due to the lack of bundled local NVMe storage, and reduced performance on advanced vector parallel tasks like multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which falls into the bottom 25% with 33.88 GB/sec.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-8 is a memory-oriented virtual instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7B12 x86_64 processor. The configuration provides 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory to achieve an 8.0 GB per vCPU density. The system does not include dedicated GPUs, integrated local storage, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. In synthetic and application testing, the instance exhibits strong single-core CPU throughput with a stress-ng score of 2,681.48 and a multi-core score of 10,764.32. Memory bandwidth reaches 69.61 GB/sec on 256 MB reads and 46.34 GB/sec on writes, supporting 7.66 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.24 GB/sec static web throughput. Given its elevated memory capacity relative to compute resources, the e2-highmem-8 provides efficient economics for in-memory caching, relational databases, data transformation pipelines, and memory-constrained enterprise services.
